Regarding the perfection of the proof by which the negation of **composition**, **change**, and **multiplicity** is explained according to the concept of the Creator, may He be exalted.
Behold, we have already explained that true, absolute unity—in which there is no change or multiplicity in any way, manner, or cause—is not found
among created beings. For all beings besides Him, may He be blessed, are **composite** <note>Hebrew: *murkavim*. In medieval philosophy, this means something made of different parts or aspects, rather than being a single, unified essence.</note>. Even if they are not composed of <term>matter and form</term><note>The Aristotelian idea that objects consist of 'matter' (the stuff) and 'form' (the essence or design).</note>, they are
composed of **substance and accident** <note>Substance is the thing itself; accidents are its non-essential properties like color or size.</note>, or of **essence and existence**, or of **potentiality and actuality** <note>Potentiality is what a thing could be; actuality is what it is right now.</note>, and what is similar to this. The Creator, may He be blessed, alone is
the **Truly One**, simple with the ultimate **simplicity**, in whom there is no composition at all—not intellectual composition,
nor sensory composition, nor imaginary composition. And this is explained by way of intellectual proof: for every composite thing requires a **composer** who joined it together,
and that composer necessarily precedes it in existence. But the Creator, may He be blessed, is the first of all beings, and has no predecessor at all. If He were composite,
He would require a composer, and that composer would precede Him, which is an absurdity. Furthermore, every composite is a <term>contingent being</term><note>Hebrew: *efshari hametziut*. Something that does not have to exist by its own nature but depends on other factors.</note> by its own nature,
for it requires its parts; if its parts or one of them were absent, the composite would cease to be. But the Creator, may He be blessed, is a <term>necessary being</term><note>Hebrew: *mechuyav hametziut*. A being whose existence is required by its very essence; it cannot *not* exist.</note>
by His own nature and does not require anything else at all. If He were composite, He would be a contingent being, and this is the opposite of what was established. Furthermore,
every composite has a limit and an end, for the parts limit one another. But the Creator, may He be blessed, is **infinite**
in all His perfection. Furthermore, every composite is subject to change, for the parts can be separated from one another. But the Creator, may He be blessed, is
entirely **unchanging**. From this it is explained that He, may He be blessed, is one, simple with the ultimate simplicity, and there is in Him no multiplicity or change.

<margin>
Gloss
</margin>

Similarly, the negation of multiplicity and change in the Creator, may He be blessed, is explained by His absolute perfection. For if there were in Him multiplicity and change,
each of the parts would be deficient on its own and would require its fellow part to complete the essence. But the Creator, may He be blessed, is perfect
with the ultimate perfection and requires nothing outside of Himself. Furthermore, if there were multiplicity in Him, each of the parts
would be distinguished from its fellow by some matter and would share with it in some matter. And the matter by which they are distinguished is different from the matter in which
they share. If so, each of them would be composed of the shared and the distinct. And this would lead to an **infinite regression** of composition <note>The logical problem where every part is made of more parts forever, which philosophers considered impossible.</note>, and this is an absurdity. Furthermore, if there were multiplicity in Him, each of the parts would be limited and finite,
as we mentioned. But the Creator, may He be blessed, is infinite. From this it is explained that He, may He be blessed, is one, simple with the ultimate
simplicity, and there is in Him no multiplicity or change at all.

---

### Explanation of the Matter of Unity

<margin>
<unclear>See the Guide for the Perplexed</unclear> <note>A reference to Maimonides' (Rambam's) seminal philosophical work, *Moreh Nevukhim*.</note>
</margin>

Behold, after the negation of composition and multiplicity in the Creator, may He be blessed, has been explained, it is proper to explain the matter of the **Unity** attributed to Him.
Know that the Unity said of Him, may He be blessed, is not like **numerical unity**, which is the beginning of number. For the
numerical "one" is a part of multiplicity and is divisible in thought. But the Creator, may He be blessed, is not a part of multiplicity and
is not subject to division at all. Rather, the Unity said of Him, may He be blessed, is the **Unity of Existence and Simplicity**.
That is to say, He, may He be blessed, is One in His existence, such that there is no other being like Him at all. And He is One in His simplicity, such that
there is no composition or multiplicity in Him at all. And this is the secret of the verse: **"Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One."** <note>original: *Shema Yisrael Adonai Eloheinu Adonai Echad* (Deuteronomy 6:4).</note>

<margin>
<unclear>Interpretation of the verse</unclear>
</margin>

For "the Lord our God" is One in His existence and One in His simplicity. And this is the great principle upon which all
the Torah and the faith rest. Anyone who believes in multiplicity or composition in the Creator, may He be blessed, is as if he denies the principle.
For he removes the Creator from the category of "Necessary Being" and places Him in the category of "Contingent Being."
May the Name, may He be exalted, lead us in the way of truth to understand the secrets of His Torah and His true Unity, Amen.

<summary>This page argues for the absolute "simplicity" and unity of God, using philosophical proofs to show that God cannot be made of parts, be finite, or be subject to change. It distinguishes God's "Unity" from the mathematical number "one," defining Him instead as the only Necessary Being.</summary>
<keywords>Divine Unity, Simplicity, Necessary Being, Contingent Being, Maimonides, Shema Israel, Monotheism, Philosophy</keywords>

<margin>
<unclear>...and so wrote the author of the *Turim*, section 158...</unclear> <note>This refers to Rabbi Jacob ben Asher, a 14th-century legal authority. Section 158 of his work, the *Arba’ah Turim*, deals with the laws of washing hands before a meal.</note>
</margin>

My children, for they are my people, and "this is the Torah which Moses set before the children of Israel" <note>quoting Deuteronomy 4:44</note> and so on. This is the explanation of the verse we mentioned above: "For the Lord’s portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance" <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. The meaning is that Israel is the actual "portion" of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and they are not under the dominion of the constellations <note>original: *mastalot*—referring to the belief that nations are governed by astrological forces, while Israel is governed directly by God</note> (as our Sages of blessed memory said: "There is no constellation <note>original: *mazal*</note> for Israel"). Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, personally guides them. This is what is meant by "For the Lord’s portion is His people"—meaning they are truly His portion and are attached to Him. He, may He be blessed, watches over them always, and His providence is constantly attached to them. 

This is also the meaning of "Jacob is the lot <note>The Hebrew word *hevel* means both a 'lot' or 'portion' and a 'rope'.</note> of His inheritance." Think of it like a rope where one end is in a person's hand and the other end is tied to something; if the person shakes the end of the rope in his hand, the other end tied to the object will also move. So it is with Israel and the Holy One, Blessed be He: they are attached to Him, may He be blessed, like this rope. If they sin down here below, it causes a "movement," as it were, up above, and they cause a blemish in their "upper root." This is the meaning of "Jacob is the rope of His inheritance"—they are truly attached to Him like this rope. 

This is also why the scripture says, "But you who held fast to the Lord your God are all alive today" <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>. This means that because you are attached to Him, may He be blessed, who is the "Life of all Life," you are alive and endure forever. Similarly, the scripture says, "For the Lord will not forsake His people for His great name’s sake, because it has pleased the Lord to make you a people for Himself" <note>1 Samuel 12:22</note>. Because His great name is associated with you, He will never forsake you. And it says, "For the Lord has chosen Jacob for Himself, Israel as His prized possession" <note>Psalms 135:4</note>. Because "Jacob chose God for himself"—meaning God's name rests upon him—therefore "Israel is His prized possession" <note>original: *segula*</note>, meaning they are a treasure from among all nations. Just as a "treasure" is something very precious and important to a king, so is Israel to the Holy One, Blessed be He. This is why the scripture says, "You shall be My treasured possession among all peoples, for all the earth is Mine" <note>Exodus 19:5</note>. This means: even though the whole earth is Mine, you shall nevertheless be My special treasure. And it says, "The Lord set His affection on your ancestors and loved them, and He chose you, their descendants, above all the nations, as it is today" <note>Deuteronomy 7:7-8</note>. This means that although the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the entire world, He only desired your holy ancestors and chose you from all nations to be His treasured people. And it says: "For you are a holy people to the Lord your God; the Lord your God has chosen you to be a people for His prized possession, out of all the peoples who are on the face of the earth" <note>Deuteronomy 7:6</note>.

### Explanation of the Psalm
->The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want<-

<margin>
Psalms 23
</margin>

King David, peace be upon him, spoke this psalm through Divine Inspiration <note>original: *Ruach HaKodesh*</note>. It is a very distinguished psalm, containing deep hints and great secrets. 

The meaning of "The Lord is my shepherd" is that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is my shepherd and guides me, just as a shepherd leads his flock and watches over them constantly so that they lack nothing. This is why it says "I shall not want"—since the Holy One, Blessed be He, is my shepherd, I will certainly not lack anything. For He, may He be blessed, feeds and sustains the entire world, and certainly He will sustain me, as He watches over me with individual providence. 

When it says, "He makes me lie down in green pastures," it means He will settle me in a place where there is much grass, so that I will have food and drink in abundance. "He leads me beside still waters" means He will lead me to a place of quiet and peaceful waters so that I can drink in tranquility and calm. "He restores my soul" means He will return my soul to its rest and serenity. "He leads me in paths of righteousness for His name's sake" means He will guide me on the straight and good path so that I may merit the Life of the World to Come <note>original: *Olam Ha-Ba*—the Jewish concept of the afterlife or the era of the resurrection</note>. All this He will do for me for the sake of His great name, which is called upon me. 

The verse "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me" means that even if I go into a place of danger or a place of darkness and gloom like the "valley of the shadow of death," I will not fear any evil thing because You are with me and watching over me always. "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me" refers to the "rod" with which You discipline me and the "staff" upon which You support me—both of them comfort me. For I know that everything You do with me is for my own good, to cleanse my sins in this world so that I may merit the Life of the World to Come.

<summary>This page provides a mystical and homiletical explanation of the unique relationship between God and the people of Israel, using the metaphor of a rope to describe their spiritual connection. It then transitions into a verse-by-verse commentary on Psalm 23, interpreting the shepherd imagery as a metaphor for God's individual providence and the purpose of suffering.</summary>

Thus far, I have proven to you in this article how much a person needs to be wise and have an open heart to all words of wisdom, and to evaluate things according to their level, so that in his eyes, the trivial and the essential are not one, for this is the way of the foolish and the senseless, according to what I have taught you in the previous chapters about the difference between a wise person and a fool.

And there is no other level for a wise person than that you will find him a wise person distinguished in his actions, in his speech, and in his thoughts, and walking in the ways of the Torah, of law and justice, and highlighting all his actions as charity and judgment. For this was the level of Solomon, the wisest of all men, who built the Holy Temple and measured all the worlds with wisdom and understanding. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him, "Why did you do this, and why did you build this house and measure it with wisdom, but in order that you should know and distinguish between every action you have done and everything created in the world? For everything was created for the sake of wisdom and understanding and the level of justice."

Therefore, Solomon was worthy to write the book of Proverbs, for in this book, he arranged and explained all the ways of man in his actions, his thoughts, and his words, and the difference between the ways of wisdom and the ways of foolishness. And as he wrote at the end of the book of Ecclesiastes, "Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of man," for in this you will distinguish between a wise person and a fool, and you will understand that the whole of man is nothing but the commandments and good deeds, and the preparation of his heart to be ready for the Torah. For all the stability of the heart is on the pillar of truth, justice, and judgment. And all who resist this path are among those madmen who kick against the way of God and His commandments, for a heart that is not aligned with the Torah cannot understand any matter of wisdom, truth, and faith, for it is blind, and in all its ways, it wanders.

Therefore, be very careful of the way of the wicked whose heart is set on silver and gold and will not be roused to understand the ways of God. And this is the level of silver and gold, that they lead man astray, for they do not rouse his heart to receive the Torah. And anyone who understands will contemplate that the <term>Intellect, the Object of Intellect, and the Intelligent Subject</term> <note>original: "ha-sekhel, ha-muskal, ve-ha-maskil." This is a foundational Aristotelian and Maimonidean concept stating that in God, the act of thinking, the thinker, and the thought are one identical unity.</note> are all one. To explain his words here would require great length, and this is not the proper place for it. However, regarding what the Rabbi wrote in that same chapter—that all of existence is of one kind—his words require further explanation. These words of his are great secrets and mysteries of the Torah, and no person can truly grasp them unless they have merited it and the secrets of the Name (blessed be He) have been revealed to them. A person must not speculate on them at all, for anyone who speculates on them is as if they were speculating about the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> itself, God forbid.

This is the secret behind the verse: *“Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place,”* and this is the secret of the <term>Unity of the Blessed Name</term> <note>original: "Yichud HaShem"</note>, the <term>Mystery of the Chariot</term> <note>original: "Sod ha-Merkavah," referring to early Jewish mystical visions of God's throne-chariot.</note>, and the mystery of the angels and the souls—all, all is one in a sufficient explanation. This is the secret of Absolute Unity. This is the secret of the verse: *“The Lord is our God, the Lord is One,”* and the secret of the verse: *“The Lord is God in the heavens above and on the earth below; there is no other.”* The meaning of "there is no other" is that there is nothing else besides Him at all. This is also the secret of the verse: *“The whole earth is full of His glory,”* and the secret of the verse: *“And You give life to them all,”* and the secret of the verse: *“The Lord reigns, the Lord has reigned, the Lord will reign forever and ever.”* This is also the secret of the verse: *“On that day the Lord shall be one and His name one,”* and the secret of the verse: *“The Lord of Hosts who dwells among the cherubim.”*

This entire matter is a great secret and a mystery of the Torah; it is not to be revealed except to those who are modest. He who has merited it will understand it through his own mind, but he who has not merited it should not investigate these matters excessively, for he will achieve nothing and could fall into heresy, God forbid. This is what the Rabbi (of blessed memory) wrote in that chapter; his words are deep matters and great secrets, and no man can grasp them except one who has merited it.

7. On another page they wrote: that every art of trials, for which one wishes to find boundaries, we will need to establish the boundaries at the beginning and not at the end. But they did the opposite, and gave it weakness, and from that moment everything changed, and the place of the beginning also changed, and it returned to the place of the end. And again, we stood before a new question: where is the place of the beginning and the place of the end? And this matter is not agreed upon by all, and to delve into the depth of the place, we must mention that every art, when it spreads, must exert effort on each and every spread, and not just on one spread, and therefore, when it comes to the point that the spread needs to bring a new necessity, this is different from the previous necessity, for now there is no total necessity here, but a limited necessity in place and time, and recently this limited necessity has also spread, and even spread to a place that is not a necessity at all.

The masters of insight also replied to this, that the matter is not so, and even though we said that the spread is limited, the rule does not say that the spread itself will be limited, because there is a difference between spread and necessity: that the spread has several occasions, and the necessity has only one occasion, and this is fixed, and it is not proper to dispute it, on condition that we begin the spread from the outset and not from the end. This means that what should have been at the end, was done at the beginning, and what should have been at the beginning, was done at the end, and all of this is a matter of patterns.

8. They further wrote on this: that if every art of trials is limited, and the place of its limitation is the beginning, and at the beginning there is necessity, then all of this depends on the good will of the practitioner, for he can change his good place to a bad place, and vice versa. And the masters of elaboration wrote on this: that the spread does not depend on the good will of the practitioner, for the practitioner is merely a tool in the hands of the spread, and he does not decide, and he does not determine, and he does not limit, and therefore all that he has to receive, he receives from others. And they further wrote on this: that all that the practitioner is compelled to do, he does as he sees fit, for he himself is a necessity and he does not need to consider another place.

The general principle: every art, when it spreads, spreads with what is compelled upon it, and if the necessity is not sufficient for it, it weakens.

1.

--- Page 53 ---
For it did not come upon him, but rather he built for himself a lasting dwelling, as we find concerning Noah, who was named Noah, saying, "This one will comfort us from our labor and from the toil of our hands." And this teaches you that Noah did not have work with burden and toil, but rather he prepared the ground, and it produced its fruits and growth without effort, unlike the former generations who worked with burden. And similarly, (Isaiah 6:13) "Though a tenth remain, it shall again be subject to burning, like an oak or a terebinth, whose stump remains when it is felled." And they interpreted "Though a tenth remain" as having returned to its good, and therefore they said, "it shall be subject to burning" (for good), for blessing is only found in something hidden from the eye. Therefore, it is connected to good. And it means to say here as well, that Moses' acquisition was in a state worthy of being hidden for good, because it was concealed and covered, whereas with Adam the First, it was in the open, and therefore it had no permanence. But Moses, whose acquisitions were in a hidden place, therefore had permanence.

And indeed, what the Sages said, "Seven things were created before the creation of the world, and these are: Torah, Repentance, the Garden of Eden, Gehinnom, the Throne of Glory, the Temple, and the name of the Messiah" - all these things are in this category, that they have existence prior to the creation of the world. For there is nothing in existence prior to the creation of the world, except things that are concealed and hidden. And even though each one has an existence in the world, nevertheless, their essence is above the world. Therefore, they have permanence, unlike things that came from the world, which do not have permanence. Furthermore, it will be explained that all things that are permanent and enduring acquisitions in ethics and wisdom are in the category of Torah and Repentance, which existed before the world was created, for their existence and essence are not from the world. And this matter is known to the enlightened, and they are two aspects. One aspect is in a place of revelation, and the second is in a hidden place. And they are the aspect of sweetness and dwelling, and the aspect of rest and settlement in this manner.

It emerges that anything that has permanence is above the world. And all things that stand upon the world's standing have a downfall. And this is the secret of "For with this shall Aaron come into the holy place." And its explanation is that he came with those things that are above the world and have no downfall. Therefore, they have permanence.

And from these eleven days come these eleven ingredients, which are holy of holies. And this is what the verse states (Leviticus 19:31) "Do not turn to the mediums or to the spiritists," because the medium (Ov) and the spiritist (Yid'oni) draw their power from this world. Therefore, it says (there) "do not defile yourselves by them," because they have no permanence.

And this is why the verse concludes (there) "I am the Lord your God," for I alone am permanent, and My attributes are not like a thing that contains a medium or a spiritist.

And this is what the verse states (Numbers 12:3) "Now the man Moses was very humble, more than anyone else on the face of the earth" - five aspects related to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, are conveyed in one verse. And this is because these five things surround Moses our teacher, peace be upon him. And they are the aspect of "Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding" (Proverbs 4:5).

And this is what Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said: "For when I return to the blessed Lord, I will dwell in You," as if to say, "for in the days of their rebellion, I did not distance myself." For I did not stand in their standing nor in their aspect, and even though I had dealings with the children of Israel, who were in rebellion, I did not come with them in their standing. And therefore it is stated (1 Samuel 15:30), "Please return with me, that I may worship the Lord your God."

And behold, Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, guarded himself from all their "standing," and regarding this it is stated, "do not defile yourselves by them." And this was the aspect of the "standing" of the children of Israel, who cannot stand (firm), and this is what the verse states (Deuteronomy 33:7) "And this he said for Judah: 'Hear, O Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people; with his hands he contended for them, and You shall be a help against his adversaries.'"

<meta>This page continues a philosophical and kabbalistic discussion regarding the nature of the "Active Intellect" and its relationship to the human soul. It bridges Aristotelian philosophy with Jewish mystical thought (Kabbalah).</meta>

<note>original: "Amnon" (אמנון)</note> Indeed, this is what was written above in the chapter on prophecy. He is called by the philosophers the <term>Active Intellect</term> <note>Hebrew: "Sekhel ha-Poel"; in medieval philosophy, this is the lowest of the ten heavenly intellects that mediates between God and the physical world</note>. He is emanated from the Name, may He be blessed, by means of the celestial spheres. He is the governor of this lowly world and the giver of forms to all existing things; he is the one who grants prophecy to the prophets and directs the human intellect toward ultimate perfection. He is called by our Sages of blessed memory the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>Divine Presence</note> or the <term>Holy Spirit</term>.

And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said: "Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, fills the whole world, so the soul fills the whole body. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, sees but is not seen, so the soul sees but is not seen. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, sustains the world, so the soul sustains the body. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, is pure, so the soul is pure. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells in the innermost chambers, so the soul dwells in the innermost chambers. Let that which possesses these five attributes come and praise Him who possesses these five attributes."

Behold, they explained in this teaching that the soul is a higher paradigm above itself, namely the Active Intellect, which is the governor of this world, sustains it, and gives it its forms. He is called the *Shekhinah*, as we have said; he is called the "Glory of the Name," may He be blessed; and he is called the "Angel of the Lord." It is of him that it is said: *Behold, I send an angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared. Pay attention to him and listen to his voice; do not rebel against him, for he will not forgive your transgression, because My name is within him.* 

It is regarding this "Glory" that it is said: *And behold, the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud.* And of this it is said: *And they saw the God of Israel, and under His feet was something like a pavement of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself.* And of this it is said: *And he [Moses] said, "Please show me Your glory." And He said, "I will cause all My goodness to pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of the Lord before you; and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show mercy on whom I will show mercy." But He said, "You cannot see My face, for no man can see Me and live." And the Lord said, "Behold, there is a place by Me, and you shall stand on the rock. And it shall be, while My glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand while I pass by. Then I will take away My hand, and you shall see My back; but My face shall not be seen."*

Behold, our teacher Moses, peace be upon him, attained a perfect perception of this Glory. Of this it is said: *He beholds the likeness of the Lord.* This is what our Sages of blessed memory meant when they said: "All the prophets looked through a <term>dull mirror</term> <note>original: "aspaklaria she-einah me'irah"; literally a mirror or lens that does not shine</note>, but our teacher Moses looked through a <term>luminous mirror</term> <note>original: "aspaklaria ha-me'irah"</note>."

Behold, this Glory is what is called the *Shekhinah*, and it is called the Holy Spirit, and it is called the Angel of the Lord, and it is called the Active Intellect, and it is called the World of Angels, and it is called

<column-break/>

the secret of the <term>Sefirah of Binah</term> <note>the divine attribute of Understanding</note>, and it is called the World of Creation, and it is called the Throne of Glory. It is emanated from the Name, may He be blessed, and it is the governor of this world, giving forms to all lowly existences. It grants prophecy to the prophets and directs the human intellect toward ultimate perfection. It is called the *Shekhinah* and the Holy Spirit, and it is called the Glory of the Name, may He be blessed. It is what is spoken of when it says: *Behold, I send an angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared. ### The Second Mode
->On the explanation of the essence of the human soul and the divisions of its powers<-

Behold, the human soul is a simple spiritual substance, not composed of the elements; it is not a body, nor is it a force within a body. It is called Intellect, and it is called Soul <note>Neshamah</note>, and it is called Spirit <note>Ruach</note>. It is that of which it is said: *And He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul.*

The rest of the Sabbath was observed and completed according to its law and without any condition at all, and even every custom that people practiced who wished to drink wine with several customs of eating wine, figs, pomegranates, etc., which is the seven species of wine, pomegranates, and figs, etc., is completely nullified. And everyone has already accustomed themselves to eating grapes, figs, pomegranates, olives, and other preserved fruits that have a peel that prevents the wine from mixing. And they would preserve much of them to eat and drink the wine and fulfill their obligation for the Sabbath day. And even though they preserved them from mixtures and they have a peel, and this prevents wine from mixtures, nevertheless their fulfillment of obligation was not achieved, because they are preserved and not from the preservers. And even grapes, figs, pomegranates, olives, and the like that have no peel at all, nevertheless they would preserve them and leave them and preserve them from wine so that there would be no wine mixture in them. And it is found that there is no wine mixture in them at all, and this is what makes them permissible for eating and drinking at night. And even though they wished to do so and drink the wine and fulfill their obligation, nevertheless they were not permitted, because their nature had changed, and the wine is not permissible unless all the things mentioned above were fulfilled in it. And from here on, one can learn about wine whose nature has changed and whose addition was praised, that even if you wish to drink it and fulfill your obligation, you will not fulfill your obligation, since its nature has changed. And this is that any wine whose nature has changed has no law of wine at all applying to it. And even wine that is preserved is not considered wine at all. And this is that any preserved wine is not considered wine at all, and there is no law of wine at all applying to it. And even the preserved wine has no law of wine at all applying to it, and any wine whose nature has changed is forbidden to drink it, and there is no law of wine at all applying to it.

He compared it with the <term>Explicit Name<note>original: "Shem HaMeforash." This refers to the hidden, powerful name of God, often associated with the 72-fold name derived from Exodus.</note></term>, as it is a vessel embroidered with every kind of wisdom and filled with the sweetness of the honeycomb which crossed over the brook of Jabbok <note>A reference to Jacob's crossing in Genesis 32, often interpreted mystically as a transition between spiritual states.</note>. And it was divided into two halves: half for God and half for man. And this is what the scripture says: "And he put it toward the half of the altar," <note>Exodus 27:5</note> equal in weight to all the sacrifices of the altar. All of it is made of fine flour, and clean fine flour from the fine flour of thought, refined sevenfold. And its end testifies to its beginning, for it is a throne of glory, exalted from the beginning, the place of our sanctuary which the Lord chose to cause His name to dwell there. "And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; on that day the Lord shall be one and His name one." <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>

As everything is found in the composition of the matter of the <term>Chariot<note>original: "Merkavah." The study of the Divine Chariot is the core of early Jewish mysticism, dealing with the vision of God's throne.</note></term>, and this is what we hinted at in the letters of <note>original: "EHYEH ASHER EHYEH"</note> **I shall be what I shall be** <note>God's name as revealed to Moses in Exodus 3:14.</note> in the secret of the Chariot. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said: "And all your desires cannot compare to her," <note>Proverbs 3:15, usually applied to the Torah.</note> even the desires of Heaven. And this is the secret of: "And it came to pass on the eighth day, that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel," <note>Leviticus 9:1</note> the secret of the Lord, to let us hear the secret of His Name. For the secret of His Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> among the children of Israel is the secret of the fifth from within; and the secret of His Presence in the House is the secret of the second; and the secret of His Name within the House is the secret of the third; and the secret of the Holy, the Holy of Holies, and the Altar is the secret of the fourth. And this is what is written: "On the eighth day Moses called Aaron," and this is what we hinted at in the composition of the Chariot in their letters and names.

And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said: When Moses ascended on high, he found the Holy One, blessed be He, tying crowns to the letters <note>This refers to the "tagin," the decorative flourishes on certain letters in a Torah scroll.</note>. And Moses said to Him: "Master of the Universe, You have a man in the world, and Akiva son of Joseph is his name, who is destined to derive from every single stroke heaps and heaps of laws." And the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: "Turn around." Moses turned around and went and sat at the end of eighteen rows <note>The rows of students in Rabbi Akiva's academy.</note>. And he did not know what they were saying until they reached a certain matter, and his students said to him: "Rabbi, from where do you know this?" and he replied: "It is a law given to Moses at Sinai." And Moses was comforted. And he returned before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said: "Master of the Universe, You have such a man, and yet You give the Torah through me?" He replied: "Be silent; thus it has risen in My thought." And he said before Him: "Master of the Universe, You have shown me his Torah, show me his reward." He said to him: "Turn around." Moses turned around and saw that they were weighing his flesh in the butcher's market <note>A reference to the martyrdom of Rabbi Akiva by the Romans.</note>. He said before Him: "Master of the Universe, this is Torah and this is its reward?" He replied: "Be silent; thus it has risen in My thought."

And this is the secret of the eighteen rows mentioned in this story, and they are the eighteen letters of the Explicit Name mentioned in the portion of *Vayissa*, *Vayavo*, *Vayet* <note>Exodus 14:19-21. This is on the day when the Children of Israel erected the Temple, the Tabernacle. On the first day of Nisan, a heavenly voice came forth and said to them: "Happy are you, Children of Israel, that you fulfill all that I commanded you. And I, too, will do for you all that I commanded them, and all that I commanded you to do for yourselves – I will do everything for you. As it is said: 'I will make it a sanctuary of equal standing, a sanctuary of equal standing as a sign.'

And I will make from it a vessel for receiving blessing, that the blessing is found in the Temple as a vessel for receiving, a vessel of testimony, a vessel of blessing, for the Temple testifies about the blessing from the Highest.
I appointed a High Priest for it from the earth; I will bring him everything found in the Temple; I will reveal to him what was destined to be and what is to be taken away in the Chosen House, and all that I have for him in two garments of testimony and two close garments according to the day, and every High Priest would give to a priest from his prophets to make them seven garments from the holy Temple of testimony, and to make them High Priests to YHVH.

YHVH YHVH YHVH YHVH, incline Your ear to this matter that I bring before You from everything found in the Temple and from everything I commanded You, and from everything I commanded You, incline Your ear to me to the matter that I am presenting before You. Incline Your ear to me to the matter that I bring before You from all that I told You and for all that I bring before You. Incline Your ear to me for every matter that I speak before You. Incline Your ear to me that I bring before You with all my heart and with all my soul. Incline Your ear to me for every matter that I speak and entrust to You, and I bring before You everything that was destined to be with two garments of testimony and two close garments according to the day, which were seven garments of testimony from the holy Temple, and to make them High Priests to YHVH.

Let me briefly say: Behold, all the prophecies that came in the future tense concerning matters of the Holy Temple and the sacrifices are conditional upon repentance and good deeds that Israel performs. And just as Jeremiah prophesied in the name of the Lord, "Behold, I am bringing upon this city and upon all its cities all the evil that I have spoken concerning it, because they stiffened their neck so as not to hear My words." And similarly, it is written in Ezekiel: "I will take the children of Israel from among the nations where they have scattered, and I will gather them from all around, and I will bring them to their land. And I will give them one heart, and a new spirit I will put within them; and I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh, so that they may walk in My statutes and keep My ordinances and do them; and they will be My people, and I will be their God." Thus, the gathering of exiles is dependent on their service/worship. And the same applies to what is stated in the book of Zechariah and the book of Malachi regarding the building of the Holy Temple and the sacrifices. And this is what the Amora explained regarding the building of the House of God when its year arrived. And this is what Rabbi Shmuel bar Rabbi Yitzchak wrote, etc.: For all prophecies for good, even if they do not contain a condition, even if they are not fulfilled, we await their fulfillment and there is no change. But prophecies of retribution, if they do not contain a condition, are destined to be nullified, and we are not to expect their fulfillment. And this is what Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi wrote, etc.: But for us, to whom the Torah was given, Torah and Mitzvah will not be nullified from us. <meta>Continuity note: This page continues the philosophical exploration of the Divine nature, moving from the human and angelic roles in unifying God's name (Page 21) to a deeper Kabbalistic analysis of how the Divine Essence remains unchanging despite the many Names and Actions perceived in the world. It aligns with the teachings of Moses Cordovero regarding the relationship between the 'Emanator' (the Source) and the 'Emanations' (the Sefirot).</meta>

We find ourselves learning that [the Divine] must be pure and refined from everything, and this precision is indicated by the term "the Exalted One," may He be blessed. One must understand and contemplate that these levels, which are called <term>Names and Epithets</term> <note>original: "Shemot ve-Kinuyim," referring to the various titles used for God in scripture, such as Elohim or Adonai</note>, are not separate from the power of the <term>Emanator</term> <note>original: "Ma’atzil," the Divine Source from which all things flow</note> within them, Heaven forbid. For in His true unity, they are all literally as one, and He does not change through the changing of the Names and the <term>Attributes</term> <note>original: "Middot," often referring to the Sefirot or Divine qualities like Mercy and Justice</note>, where one is not distinct from the other.

Just as the water and fire within a coal are drawn after the flame—for they act within the flame through many varied actions beyond investigation—so too these levels are found within their Emanator like the power found within the coal before the flame emerges. When the flame emerges into action, the change is in the flame, not within the coal. All this is to understand and contemplate that there is no change in the Emanator; He is one and unique in the beauty of His unity. Even though the Names and Epithets are many, there is no change in their Emanator at all.

All this serves to indicate the excellence of the levels: they act through the changing will of the <term>recipients</term> <note>the created beings who receive Divine influence</note>, but not through the will of the Emanator, for He is equal toward all. All changes are in the order of the levels according to the action that emerges from them. They are literally the Godhead, and He is one with all of them, and they are one with Him without any change, separation, or multiplicity at all. All this is to show and reveal that the Names and Epithets are these levels, and they are called the Names of the Emanator because He acts through them in ways that indicate that specific Name. For example: the name <term>El</term> <note>original: "El," often associated with the attribute of Kindness</note> indicates <term>Kindness</term> <note>original: "Chesed"</note>, and the name <term>Elohim</term> indicates <term>Judgment</term> <note>original: "Din"</note>. Nevertheless, He, may He be exalted, is within them and within their value; He is one with all of them, and they are one with Him, unified in Him with the ultimate unity in which there is no separation or change. It is a complete, simple unity, free from all types of compositions, species, or categories. He is the one who emanates everything from <term>nothingness into being</term> <note>original: "mi-ayin le-yesh"</note>, the power of all existing things, and all are literally as one in the secret of His unity.

As for what is said in many places regarding Names, Epithets, and the changing of Attributes—this is not, Heaven forbid, any change in the Emanator, may He be blessed. Rather, it is all in relation to the recipients. Through them, the change is seen in the Attributes and Names, for He, may He be blessed, performs all actions according to the deeds of those below. According to His action found among those below—whether it be Judgment, Kindness, Mercy, Greatness, Strength, Beauty, or the other levels called Names and Epithets—that Actor will be called by that name in relation to the recipients; otherwise, He would not be called so.

<meta>catchword: and is called</meta>
<margin>Intelligence <unclear>...</unclear></margin>

<column-break/>

It is found, therefore, that the change which seems to come from His side, may He be blessed, is actually the change that occurs in His actions, not in His essence. It is clear that change occurs in existing things from the side of <term>matter</term>. In all the Work of Creation that was renewed, no change was renewed, Heaven forbid, in His essence; for everything is from Him without change, relative to the changing paths in the reality of the recipients.

Just as the sun, which shines upon the face of the earth, performs changing actions upon changing substances—it melts wax, hardens clay, whitens a garment, and blackens the face of the laundryman—this is not due to the essence of the sun, but only in relation to the recipients. So too is this matter regarding Him, may He be blessed: He performs many changes in created beings, yet never changes in Himself. This is what the scripture means: *“I, the Lord, have not changed”* <note>Malachi 3:6</note>. For He is the shining sun, emanating change to the created beings from their own side and from the side of the <term>vessels</term> <note>original: "keilim," the structures that catch and define Divine light</note> that receive the change. He, may He be blessed, is one in relation to the action proceeding from Him without any change at all, for the change is in the created beings, not in the Creator, may He be blessed.

So too the scripture says: *“You were He before the world was created, and You are He after the world was created,”* <note>From the morning liturgy, based on the Midrash</note> because He has no change at all, neither before creation nor after creation. For everything exists from Him and from His thought, and He is one with the thought, for His thought is not outside of Him. Everything exists within the thought; He watches, observes, and sees everything in His thought, for He, the Thought, and the Knowledge are all one thing, and there is no change in Him at all.

Even though Names, Epithets, and changes of Attributes and actions are mentioned, it is all in relation to the created beings, which are the levels that receive the flow and the light from Him, may He be blessed. These are the Attributes whose action changes, and all the change is in them, not in their Emanator, for they are the vessels that receive the change, not He, may He be blessed. Thus the scripture says: *“For the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by Him actions are weighed”* <note>1 Samuel 2:3</note>—all in relation to the levels whose actions in created beings are relative to change. For the Attributes are nothing other than His actions spreading out from Him into this lowly existence according to the vessels that receive His flow and light. It has thus been explained that there is no change in Him, Heaven forbid, but everything is in relation to the recipients. He is the Creator of all these changes, and even though they change, the change is not in Him, may He be blessed; for everything is by a single word and a simple will, and there is no change in His thought or His action.

Through the <term>overflow<note>Hebrew: *Shefa*. In medieval philosophy, this refers to the divine influence or energy that "pours out" from the Source to sustain the universe.</note></term> of the Intellect, these things come to them, as does the equilibrium of their bodies. This is because the <term>First Intellect<note>Hebrew: *Ha-Sekhel ha-Rishon*. Therefore, it is necessary to know and learn that in the traditional way, and especially in the way of wisdom, and in many forms of interpretations and in many places, the Scripture speaks things, and among them are examinations, aspects, and details whose profound depth and immense significance have no measure or special value except in the general and comprehensive way. And it is stated in a general way and what relates to it by way of hint, or the great or small difference, and also what relates to it in many ways. Therefore, the wise person engaged in this must understand and comprehend in every way and concerning every matter through the well-placed and well-reasoned explanation, and what pertains to each and every thing in its name and essence. For the depth of the matter of these things is exceedingly sublime, and no human intellect can comprehend the depth of the matter, but only wisdom alone, which stands at the pinnacle of the world, above everything of the world of action and deed. Therefore, we ask of the Name, blessed be His Name, that He open our eyes and our hearts and also our minds to understand and comprehend in this the profound essence of wisdom, and especially in this clear and pleasing book of Names, which are emanation (Atzilut), and also of glory and majesty, in which everything ascends and also descends, every matter and every thing, of above and of below, and they have great depth, depth from this, depth from that. And so it truly is the matter.
